source_text: Item Saturus in alia porta Pudentem militem exhortabatur dicens: Ad summam, inquit, certe, sicut praesumpsi et praedixi, nullam usque adhuc bestiam sensi. Et nunc de toto corde credas: ecce prodeo illo, et ab uno morsu leopardi consumor. Et statim in fine spectaculi, leopardo eiecto, de uno morsu tanto perfusus est sanguine, ut populus reuertenti illi secundi baptismatis testimonium reclamauerit: Saluum lotum, saluum lotum. Plane utique saluus erat qui hoc modo lauerat. Tunc Pudenti militi: Uale, inquit, memor fidei et mei; et haec te non conturbent, sed confirment. Simulque ansulam de digito eius petiit, et uulneri suo mersam reddidit ei hereditatem, pignus relinquens illi et memoriam sanguinis. Exinde iam exanimis prosternitur cum ceteris ad iugulationem solito loco. Et cum populus illos in medio postularet, ut gladio penetranti in eorum corpore oculos suos comites homicidii adiungerent, ultro surrexerunt et se quo uolebat populus transtulerunt, ante iam osculati inuicem, ut martyrium per solemnia pacis consummarent. Ceteri quidem inmobiles et cum silentio ferrum receperunt: multo magis Saturus, qui et prior ascenderat, prior reddidit spiritum; nam et Perpetuam sustinebat. Perpetua autem, ut aliquid doloris gustaret, inter ossa conpuncta exululauit, et errantem dexteram tirunculi gladiatoris ipsa in iugulum suum transtulit. Fortasse tanta femina aliter non potuisset occidi, quae ab inmundo spiritu timebatur, nisi ipsa uoluisset. O fortissimi ac beatissimi martyres! O uere uocati et electi in gloriam domini nostri Iesu Christi! Quam qui magnificat et honorificat et adorat, utique et haec non minora ueteribus exempla in aedificationem ecclesiae legere debet, ut nouae quoque uirtutes unum et eundem semper spiritum sanctum usque adhuc operari testificentur omnipotentem deum patrem et filium eius Iesum Christum dominum nostrum, cui est claritas et immensa potestas in saecula saeculorum, amen.
thought_title: The last deaths and the call to read them
orientation: The editor narrates the final killings of Saturus, Perpetua, and the others in the arena and then closes the work.
pass_a_gloss: Also Saturus at another gate was encouraging Pudens the soldier, saying: To sum up, he said, surely, just as I presumed and foretold, I have felt no wild beast up to now. And now may you believe from whole heart: behold I go forth to that one, and by one bite of a leopard I am consumed. And immediately at the end of the public games, with a leopard let out, from one bite he was drenched with so much blood that the people shouted back to him as he returned the testimony of a second baptism: One saved, washed, one saved, washed. Plainly indeed saved was he who had washed in this way. Then to Pudens the soldier: Farewell, he said, remembering the faith and me; and may these things not disturb you, but strengthen you. And at the same time he asked for the little ring from his finger, and dipped in his own wound he gave it back to him as an inheritance, leaving to him a pledge and a memory of blood. From there now lifeless he is thrown down with the rest for throat-cutting in the usual place. And when the people demanded them in the middle, so that with a sword driving through into their body they might join their own eyes as companions of murder, of their own accord they rose up and moved themselves to where the people wanted, having already kissed one another before, so that they might complete their martyrdom through the rites of peace. The rest indeed motionless and with silence received the iron: much more Saturus, who also had gone up first, first gave back his spirit; for he was also sustaining Perpetua. But Perpetua, so that she might taste something of pain, pierced between bones shrieked out, and the wandering right hand of the untrained gladiator she herself transferred to her own throat. Perhaps so great a woman could not have been killed otherwise, who was feared by the unclean spirit, unless she herself had willed it. O most brave and most blessed martyrs! O truly called and chosen into the glory of our lord Jesus Christ! Whoever magnifies and honors and worships which glory, indeed also ought to read these examples not lesser than the ancient ones for the building up of the church, so that new powers also may bear witness that one and the same Holy Spirit works always up to still, God the Father almighty and his son Jesus Christ our lord, to whom is brightness and immense power into ages of ages, amen.

choices.why: brief glossary fixes bestiae as wild beasts for arena animals
brief glossary fixes baptismus as baptism including blood as second wash
brief contrasts passio/martyrdom as faithful witness unto death, not general suffering
brief glossary fixes spiritus sanctus as Holy Spirit

choices.english: for the building up of the church
choices.why: brief glossary fixes ecclesia as church edified by reading

pass_b_english: At the other gate, Saturus was encouraging Pudens the soldier. He said: "In short, you can be sure that, just as I claimed beforehand and foretold, I have felt no wild beast at all up to now. And now believe with all your heart. Look, I am going out there, and one bite of the leopard will finish me." Then at once, near the close of the show, the leopard was let loose, and one bite covered him with so much blood that the crowd shouted to him as he came back with the testimony of a second baptism: "Saved and washed, saved and washed." He was plainly saved, for he had washed himself in this way. Then he said to Pudens the soldier: "Farewell. Remember the faith, and remember me. Do not let these things trouble you. Let them make you strong." At the same time he asked for the little ring from Pudens's finger, dipped it in his own wound, and gave it back to him as an inheritance, leaving him a pledge of his blood to remember him by.

From that moment he lay drained of life and threw himself down with the rest in the usual place for the cutting of their throats. When the crowd demanded them in the center, so that the people could join their own eyes to the murder as the sword sank into each body, they rose on their own and moved to whatever spot the crowd wanted. They had already kissed one another, so that they would complete their martyrdom with the rites of peace. The rest received the steel motionless and in silence. Saturus did so even more. He had gone up first, and he gave up his spirit first, for he was also holding Perpetua up. But Perpetua, pierced between the bones, cried out, that she might taste something of the pain. Then she herself guided the straying right hand of the young gladiator to her own throat. Perhaps so great a woman, who was feared by the unclean spirit, could not have been killed in any other way unless she herself had willed it.

O bravest and most blessed martyrs. O truly called and chosen into the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. Whoever magnifies and honors and adores that glory should surely read these recent deeds, no less than the ancient models, for the building up of the church. In this way these new acts of power will also testify to God the Father Almighty and His Son Jesus Christ our Lord that one and the same Holy Spirit is still at work. To Him belong glory and immeasurable power forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: and that God the Father Almighty and His Son Jesus Christ our Lord endure
problems.source_quote: testificentur omnipotentem deum patrem et filium eius Iesum Christum dominum nostrum
problems.why: The source has no verb 'endure'. The new acts of power testify to almighty God and his Son, who are the object of testimony, and that claim is not that they endure.
problems.fix: these new acts of power will also testify to almighty God the Father and his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

problems.quote: Whoever magnifies and honors and adores the Lord
problems.source_quote: Quam qui magnificat et honorificat et adorat
problems.why: Quam refers to gloriam just named, not the Lord; object changed.
problems.fix: Whoever magnifies and honors and adores that glory
problems.ruling: "Quam qui magnificat" – Quam is relative pronoun for 'gloriam'; English makes 'the Lord' the object, shifting what is magnified and adored.

problems.quote: felt a stab between the bones and cried out, so that she would taste something of the pain.
problems.source_quote: ut aliquid doloris gustaret, inter ossa conpuncta exululauit
problems.why: Latin tasting is purpose of the piercing, not result of crying out.
problems.fix: pierced between the bones she cried out, that she might taste something of pain.
problems.ruling: "ut aliquid doloris gustaret" states purpose of being pierced; English attaches it to crying out and makes 'felt a stab' the cause, altering the sense.

edits.old: Whoever magnifies and honors and adores the Lord
edits.new: Whoever magnifies and honors and adores that glory

edits.old: But Perpetua felt a stab between the bones and cried out, so that she would taste something of the pain.
edits.new: But Perpetua, pierced between the bones, cried out, that she might taste something of the pain.

edits.old: will also testify that one and the same Holy Spirit is still at work, and that God the Father Almighty and His Son Jesus Christ our Lord endure.
edits.new: will also testify to God the Father Almighty and His Son Jesus Christ our Lord that one and the same Holy Spirit is still at work.

fixed: addition: removed added 'endure'; God the Father and Son are object of testimony (testificentur omnipotentem deum patrem et filium...), not subjects of a second that-clause.
mistranslation: changed 'the Lord' to 'that glory' because quam refers to gloriam, feminine, not dominum.
modality: changed result 'so that she would taste' to purpose 'that she might taste' and 'felt a stab' to 'pierced' for inter ossa conpuncta; tasting (ut gustaret) is purpose of piercing.

last_rejected.quote: for he was also holding Perpetua up
last_rejected.why: Here sustinebat means 'was waiting for'. The reason he died first is that he was waiting for Perpetua. 'Holding up' gives a physical act the source doesn't state.
last_rejected.fix: he gave up his spirit first, for he was waiting for Perpetua too.
last_rejected.ruling: sustinebat normally means support/hold up, so holding Perpetuam sustinebat is within range
